outputs.L2: A video encoding apparatus includes a generation unit that forms a prediction block for a current prediction unit based on a reference index and a motion vector of the current prediction unit, and also produces a residual block representing the difference between the current prediction unit and the prediction block. The apparatus further includes a transform unit that converts the residual block into a transform block, and a quantization unit that quantizes the coefficients of the transform block with a quantization parameter to produce a quantization block. The quantization unit creates the quantization block by choosing two usable effective quantization parameters from among the left, upper, and previous quantization parameters, in accordance with a predetermined priority order assigned to those parameters, and applying the average of the selected two effective quantization parameters. An entropy coding unit then entropy-encodes the quantization block according to a scan pattern. outputs.L3:
The device encodes video data by first generating a prediction block for a current prediction unit. To generate the prediction block, the device uses a reference index and a motion vector that identify a reference region in a previously encoded or decoded picture. The prediction block is then compared with the current prediction unit, and the difference between them is used to generate a residual block. This residual block represents the portion of the current prediction unit that is not accurately predicted by the reference data.

The residual block is then processed by a transformer. The transformer converts the residual block from the spatial domain into a transform block, typically representing the residual information as a set of transform coefficients. These coefficients compact the residual energy and make the data more suitable for compression.

Next, the transform block coefficients are quantized. The quantization process uses a quantization parameter that is derived from the average of two available effective quantization parameters. These effective quantization parameters are selected from candidate parameters associated with a left neighboring block, an upper neighboring block, and a previously used parameter. When selecting the two available effective quantization parameters, the device follows a predetermined priority order among the left, upper, and previous parameters. The resulting averaged value is used to determine the quantization parameter applied to the transform coefficients, thereby producing a quantization block.

The quantization block is then entropy-coded. During entropy coding, the quantized coefficients are arranged and processed according to a scan pattern. The scan pattern defines the order in which the coefficients are read and encoded, allowing the encoder to represent the quantized data efficiently.

In addition, the motion vector used for prediction is encoded using a motion vector predictor. The predictor is selected from available effective motion vector candidates, which may include spatial motion vector candidates derived from neighboring blocks or temporal motion vector candidates derived from reference pictures. Once the appropriate predictor is selected, the motion vector can be encoded relative to that predictor. The same scan pattern used for the quantization block is also applied consistently to each subset of quantized coefficients, ensuring uniform coefficient ordering during entropy coding.
outputs.L4:
A video encoding device processes an input video signal by dividing a picture into coding units or blocks and encoding each block using prediction, transform, quantization, and entropy-coding operations. For a current block to be encoded, the device generates a prediction block using either intra prediction, based on spatially neighboring samples within the same picture, or inter prediction, based on motion-compensated samples from one or more previously encoded reference pictures. The device then generates a residual block by subtracting the prediction block from the original current block. The residual block represents the difference between the original image information and the predicted image information.

The residual block is transformed to produce transform coefficients that concentrate the residual energy into a frequency-domain representation. These transform coefficients are then quantized according to a quantization parameter, producing a quantization block that contains quantized transform coefficients. The quantization parameter may affect the degree of compression and the amount of distortion introduced during encoding. A smaller quantization parameter generally preserves more detail but requires more bits, while a larger quantization parameter generally reduces the bit rate but may reduce reconstructed image quality.

To improve consistency in determining the quantization parameter for a current block, the encoder may derive an effective quantization parameter using neighboring blocks that have already been encoded. When two neighboring effective quantization parameters are available, the encoder may average the two values to determine the effective quantization parameter for the current block. The neighboring parameters may be selected according to a priority order, so that reliable spatially adjacent or otherwise relevant blocks are used first. This prioritized selection and averaging process can reduce abrupt quantization changes between adjacent blocks and can improve visual consistency across a picture.

The encoder also performs motion vector prediction when inter prediction is used. A motion vector for the current block indicates a displacement between the current block and a corresponding prediction region in a reference picture. Rather than coding the full motion vector directly, the encoder may determine a motion vector predictor and encode a difference between the actual motion vector and the predictor. The predictor may be selected from spatial motion vector candidates associated with neighboring blocks in the current picture or from temporal motion vector candidates associated with corresponding blocks in reference pictures. By selecting an appropriate spatial or temporal motion vector predictor, the encoder can reduce the number of bits needed to represent motion information while maintaining accurate prediction.

After quantization, the quantized transform coefficients in the quantization block are entropy-coded. Before entropy coding, the coefficients may be arranged according to a scan pattern, such as a diagonal, horizontal, or vertical scan order. The scan pattern determines the order in which coefficients are processed and coded. In some cases, the quantization block may be divided into multiple coefficient subsets. The encoder applies the same scan pattern across these coefficient subsets so that coefficient ordering remains consistent throughout the block. This consistent scanning can simplify coding decisions and improve entropy-coding performance, particularly when coefficient distributions are predictable within the selected scan order.

The entropy-coding process converts syntax elements associated with the current block into a compressed bitstream. These syntax elements may include quantized coefficient values, significance flags, motion vector difference information, prediction mode information, reference picture indices, quantization parameter information, and other coding parameters. By using prioritized neighboring quantization parameters, efficient motion vector prediction, and consistent scan patterns for coefficient subsets, the encoding device can produce a bitstream that is both compact and reliably decodable.

Overall, the approach improves video compression efficiency and encoding consistency. Averaging two available effective quantization parameters helps provide stable quantization behavior across neighboring blocks. Selecting spatial or temporal motion vector predictors reduces the amount of motion information that must be coded. Applying the same scan pattern across coefficient subsets improves regularity in coefficient coding. Together, these techniques allow the video encoding device to reduce bit rate while preserving reconstructed video quality and maintaining compatibility with structured block-based video coding processes.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a legalistic technical description of a video encoder invention where the quantization parameter is derived from two available neighboring QPs among left, upper, and previous QPs, and motion vectors are encoded using spatial or temporal candidates.
counterfactuals.output:
A video encoding apparatus and method are provided for compressing a sequence of pictures by performing predictive coding, transform coding, quantization, entropy coding, and motion-vector coding. The apparatus includes a prediction unit, a transform and quantization unit, a quantization-parameter derivation unit, a motion-information coding unit, and an entropy coding unit.

In one embodiment, a current coding unit, coding block, prediction unit, or other block-based coding region is encoded using a quantization parameter (“QP”) that is not signaled in its entirety, but is derived at least in part from neighboring QP information. For the current block, the encoder identifies a plurality of neighboring QP candidates, including at least: a left-neighbor QP associated with a block spatially adjacent to a left side of the current block; an upper-neighbor QP associated with a block spatially adjacent to an upper side of the current block; and a previous QP associated with a previously encoded block in coding order, slice order, tile order, coding-tree order, or another predetermined processing order.

The quantization-parameter derivation unit determines availability of the left-neighbor QP, the upper-neighbor QP, and the previous QP according to predetermined availability conditions. Such conditions may include whether the corresponding neighboring block exists, whether the neighboring block belongs to a same slice, tile, picture region, coding-tree unit, or independently decodable segment, whether the neighboring block has already been encoded, and whether the neighboring block is permitted for use as a prediction source under applicable coding constraints.

When three candidate QPs comprising the left-neighbor QP, upper-neighbor QP, and previous QP are considered, and only two of the candidates are available for use, the quantization-parameter derivation unit derives a predicted QP for the current block from the two available neighboring QPs. In one implementation, the predicted QP is generated as an average, rounded average, weighted average, median-equivalent value, minimum, maximum, or other deterministic function of the two available QPs. In another implementation, the predicted QP is derived by selecting one of the two available QPs according to a priority rule or coding-mode-dependent rule. The derived predicted QP may be used directly as the QP of the current block, or may be combined with a signaled QP delta to obtain the final QP for the current block.

For example, if the left-neighbor QP and upper-neighbor QP are available and the previous QP is unavailable, the predicted QP may be derived from the left-neighbor QP and the upper-neighbor QP. If the left-neighbor QP and previous QP are available and the upper-neighbor QP is unavailable, the predicted QP may be derived from the left-neighbor QP and the previous QP. If the upper-neighbor QP and previous QP are available and the left-neighbor QP is unavailable, the predicted QP may be derived from the upper-neighbor QP and the previous QP. The use of exactly two available QPs enables robust QP prediction at picture boundaries, slice boundaries, tile boundaries, or other regions where one of the neighboring QPs cannot be used.

The encoder may further encode a residual signal by transforming a difference between an original block and a predicted block, quantizing transform coefficients using the final QP derived for the current block, and entropy coding quantized coefficient information. The QP delta, if present, may be entropy coded together with syntax elements identifying block partitioning, prediction mode, transform information, and coefficient data.

The prediction unit may generate inter-predicted blocks using motion information. For a current block coded in an inter-prediction mode, the motion-information coding unit constructs one or more motion-vector candidate lists. The candidate lists may include spatial motion-vector candidates obtained from neighboring blocks adjacent to the current block, including one or more left, upper, upper-right, lower-left, or upper-left neighboring blocks. The candidate lists may also include temporal motion-vector candidates derived from a reference picture different from the current picture, such as a collocated block or a block spatially related to the current block in a previously decoded or previously encoded picture.

The encoder determines motion information for the current block, including at least one motion vector and one or more reference-picture indices. The motion vector may be represented by selecting a candidate from a spatial candidate list or a temporal candidate list, or from a combined list including both spatial and temporal candidates. The encoder may signal an index identifying the selected candidate, and may further signal a motion-vector difference when the selected candidate is used as a predictor rather than as a complete motion description. In a merge mode, skip mode, or analogous mode, the selected spatial or temporal candidate may provide motion information without signaling a separate motion-vector difference. In an advanced motion-vector prediction mode, the selected candidate may provide a motion-vector predictor, and a residual motion-vector difference may be encoded.

The motion-information coding unit may perform pruning or redundancy checking among the spatial and temporal candidates so that duplicate candidates are removed or deprioritized. Candidate ordering may be predetermined or adaptively determined based on availability, prediction direction, reference picture list, reference index, block size, coding mode, or other syntax or context information. A temporal candidate may be scaled according to temporal distance between the current picture, the reference picture used by the current block, and the picture from which the temporal candidate is derived.

In operation, the encoder processes the current block by determining whether the block is intra-predicted or inter-predicted. For inter prediction, the encoder forms motion-vector candidate information from available spatial and/or temporal neighboring blocks, selects or derives motion information for the current block, generates a motion-compensated prediction block, and encodes any residual data. Independently, or in coordination with rate-control and coding-mode decisions, the encoder derives the QP for the current block from two available neighboring QPs selected from the left-neighbor QP, the upper-neighbor QP, and the previous QP, and applies the resulting QP to quantization of transform coefficients associated with the current block.

The described arrangement reduces signaling overhead associated with QP representation while preserving adaptability of quantization across spatially and temporally varying picture content. By deriving the current QP from two available neighboring QPs among left, upper, and previous QPs, the encoder provides stable QP prediction even when one neighboring QP is unavailable. Furthermore, by encoding motion vectors using spatial or temporal motion-vector candidates, the encoder reduces motion-information bitrate while maintaining efficient inter-picture prediction. The combination of neighboring-QP-based quantization control and candidate-based motion-vector coding improves compression efficiency while maintaining compatibility with block-based hybrid video coding architectures.
